subject: generative-ui
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, the three load-bearing contracts, Generation Mechanisms Compared, Component Palette Design, the two render substrates, the render pipeline, streaming discipline, the interaction loop, the hosted-widget data channel, Verification, Do NOT Use When).

cases.scenario: An assistant emits UI specs as free-form JSON via a 'please respond with JSON' prompt, then JSON.parse + try/catch + retry. In production ~6% of turns hit a retry loop because the model omits required fields or invents prop shapes.
cases.context: The provider supports both structured outputs and strict tool calling; the team thinks 'we already validate, so we're fine.'
cases.question: How should the agent fix the generation-constraint contract?
expected_flags: Free-form JSON + post-validation is prototype-grade, not a production render contract; valid JSON is not schema adherence
Switch to provider-native structured output or strict/schema-enforced tool calling (grammar-constrained decoding)
This forces every emission to be a valid schema instance, eliminating the retry loops
Keep app-side validation as defense-in-depth, but the constraint must be enforced at decode
expected_fix_hints: Adopt OpenAI Structured Outputs / Gemini response schema / Anthropic strict tool use for the palette
Treat the component schema as the response_format / tool argument schema
absent_signals: Do not keep best-effort JSON + retry as the production mechanism
Do not treat post-validation alone as sufficient

cases.scenario: A render pipeline maps the model's emitted spec straight to components and passes spec.props through, including an image `src` and a link `href`, trusting that 'the schema already validated it.'
cases.context: Specs can be influenced by retrieved/attacker-controlled content the model summarized.
cases.question: What is wrong and how should the agent harden the pipeline?
expected_flags: Schema validity describes structure, not acceptable content — it does not authorize rendering
Per-component safety policy is missing: origin allowlist for image URLs, link/target sanitization, content-length caps, finite recursion depth
The model's emission alone authorizes nothing; the pipeline must validate props independently and apply safety policy before invoking a component
Notes the threat surface includes rendering attacker-influenced output (read with prompt-injection-defense)
expected_fix_hints: Add the safety-policy step: allowlist image origins, sanitize hrefs, bound lengths, cap nesting depth
Validate props against the component's runtime schema as defense in depth
absent_signals: Do not treat schema validity as authorization to render
Do not pass model-supplied URLs/HTML straight into the DOM

cases.scenario: A team building inside a ChatGPT-Apps-style host wants to ship a rich interactive map widget with third-party JS, and is hand-rolling a typed-component registry that maps a 'map' spec to their own React component — then asking how to let the model inject custom map JS.
cases.context: The widget needs third-party/interactive code the host does not fully trust; the team is mixing substrates.
cases.question: Which render substrate fits, and how should safety be framed?
expected_flags: For rich/interactive third-party code, the sandboxed-iframe substrate fits (MCP Apps / OpenAI Apps SDK / MCP-UI), not a typed-component tree
Safety comes from isolation + host mediation: the iframe can't reach parent DOM/cookies/storage; the host enforces CSP/domain policy and proxies tool calls
The HTML resource is DEVELOPER-authored once; the model never writes the map JS — it emits a tool call selecting the resource + data
Explicitly name the substrate and its safety basis (restriction vs isolation); do not let the model inject custom JS
expected_fix_hints: Author the map UI as a ui:// resource rendered in a sandboxed iframe with a host-controlled CSP/domain allowlist
Feed model data over the postMessage/JSON-RPC bridge; proxy any tool calls through host authorization
absent_signals: Do not let the model author/inject the map JS
Do not assume host sandboxing removes the need for schema, CSP, origin, and action policy

cases.scenario: To reduce latency, a chat UI renders components incrementally from partial tool-argument deltas, mounting interactive buttons as soon as the discriminator is known — before the full spec validates.
cases.context: Some specs include a destructive 'confirm cancel' action whose guard fields arrive late in the stream.
cases.question: What is the risk and what discipline should the agent enforce?
expected_flags: Partial output is a latency affordance, not a render authorization
A partial spec may drive only visibly-provisional UI (skeleton/optimistic shell); it must be visibly non-final
Final/interactive/side-effecting components mount only after the full spec passes the same schema+props+safety validation
Never wire interaction to a provisional render; mounting a destructive action before its guard fields exist is the danger
expected_fix_hints: Render skeletons off the discriminator; commit the interactive render only after completed validation
absent_signals: Do not mount interactive/side-effecting components off half-parsed deltas
Do not treat partial deltas as final authority

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Partial output is a latency affordance, not a render authorization.
Surfaces this expected flag: A partial spec may drive only visibly-provisional UI (skeleton/optimistic shell); it must be visibly non-final.
Surfaces this expected flag: Final/interactive/side-effecting components mount only after the full spec passes the same schema+props+safety validation.
Surfaces this expected flag: Never wire interaction to a provisional render; mounting a destructive action before its guard fields exist is the danger.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Render skeletons off the discriminator; commit the interactive render only after completed validation.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Wire buttons/inputs live only post-validation.

Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not treat partial deltas as final authority.

cases.scenario: A model-rendered card has a 'Delete account' button whose onClick directly calls the delete API. The team reasons 'the user clicked it, so it's authorized.'
cases.context: The card content can be influenced by summarized untrusted input.
cases.question: How should the agent redesign the action handling?
expected_flags: A click is a user signal, not authorization for a destructive operation
The click should produce a structured event the model reasons about; the destructive effect is a SEPARATE tool call gated by user identity
Route capability delegation through the host with user consent (MCP Apps / Apps SDK), with normal authorization, idempotency, and audit controls
Auto-executing destructive actions on a rendered-component click is a prompt-injection-defense failure waiting to happen
expected_fix_hints: Replace direct onClick→API with an emitted typed event → model/tool turn → user-identity-gated tool call
Add a gated-action HITL state (confirmation) before the destructive effect
absent_signals: Do not auto-execute the delete from the click
Do not treat the click as authorization

cases.scenario: A hosted-widget search tool stuffs the entire 5,000-row result set plus pagination cursors into the tool result that the model reads, then complains about token cost and the model getting steered by bulk data.
cases.context: Building on the OpenAI Apps SDK / MCP Apps data-channel shape (structuredContent / content / _meta).
cases.question: How should the agent split the tool-result data?
expected_flags: Put render-only / bulk / untrusted data the model should not see or pay tokens for in `_meta` (component-only, never enters model context)
Put only what the model must reason about next turn in `structuredContent`/`content`
_meta keeps the large payload out of the context window and keeps untrusted bulk data from steering the model
Still protect _meta per the component's threat model (it is visible to the component/browser) and keep the host's per-widget CSP/domain allowlist
expected_fix_hints: Move the full result set + cursors into _meta; surface a summary the model reasons about in structuredContent
Enforce the per-widget domain/CSP allowlist on the resource
absent_signals: Do not push bulk render-only data into the model-visible channels
Do not assume host sandboxing removes the need for the channel split

cases.scenario: A team has a single, known, repeated checkout flow with fixed steps and wants to make it 'generative UI' by having the model decide the layout of each step on every load. They also ask the agent to design the HTTP API endpoint shape for the orders resource as part of this.
cases.context: The workflow is fixed and repeated; the endpoint design is a separate concern the team folds in.
cases.question: How should the agent scope this request?
expected_flags: For known, repeated workflows, traditional UI design is the better fit — generative UI is for open-ended assistant responses where the right presentation varies per question
Making a fixed checkout 'generative' adds nondeterminism and risk for no benefit
Designing the HTTP endpoint shape is api-design, not this skill (this skill owns the model→renderer schema, a different actor pair)
Correctly redirects both rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Keep the fixed checkout as deterministic traditional UI
Route the orders endpoint design to api-design
absent_signals: Do not recommend generative UI for the fixed repeated workflow
Do not design the HTTP API endpoint as if it were the generative-UI schema
